description: Modern, lightweight and multi-cluster Kubernetes GUI. Available on Windows, macOS and Linux.

summary.one_liner: Aptakube is a lightweight, multi-cluster desktop GUI for Kubernetes, built with Tauri and Rust, that reads your existing kubeconfig.
summary.what_it_does: Aptakube connects a desktop app directly to the API server of each Kubernetes cluster in your kubeconfig, so you can view and manage several clusters at once. It offers a workload overview that highlights failing pods, broken deployments, undersized containers, and warning events. A log viewer streams live and historical logs from multiple pods or containers together, with filtering and export. It shows CPU and memory metrics for nodes and workloads (works with metrics-server and Prometheus) and provides one-click port forwarding. Resources can be viewed in a human-friendly layout or as full YAML for editing, with quick actions such as restart, scale, and delete, plus a resource diff tool for comparing objects across clusters or namespaces.
use_cases: manage multiple Kubernetes clusters from one app
find failing pods and broken deployments
stream logs from many pods at once
port-forward to a pod without kubectl syntax
compare resource configs for drift between clusters
edit Kubernetes YAML in a desktop GUI
monitor pod and node CPU and memory
how_to_run: Download the installer for your platform from the Download section (macOS, Windows 10+ x64, or Linux .deb, .rpm, .AppImage)
notable: Built with Tauri rather than Electron, for a small install and fast startup
Zero-config: reads existing kubeconfig without changing kubectl workflow
Runs locally and connects directly to the cluster API; nothing installed on the cluster
Aggregated log viewer across multiple pods and containers
Multi-tab interface for resources, logs, and views side by side
caveats: Desktop app only, available for Windows, macOS and Linux; no web or server version is described
